name: The Canary Palm of San Servolo
age_estimate: not individually dated; described as one of the island's 'very ancient trees'
verified_sources: data/registers/italy-masaf.json (sheet_id 01/L736/VE/05, comune Venezia, locality Isola San Servolo, girth 188 cm, height 10.5 m)
access: Free, public park; separate paid ticket for the Museo del Manicomio
transport: Vaporetto line 20 from San Zaccaria, about 10 minutes
verify_notes: Individual MASAF register sheet (not a 'group' entry) gives tree-level coordinates and measurements: girth 188 cm, height 10.5 m. APGI (Associazione Parchi e Giardini Italiani), an independent garden-heritage source, describes the island's park as holding 'Canary palms' among its ancient trees and specifically says a Canary palm 'welcomes visitors as soon as they disembark on the island' (dalla palma delle Canarie, che ci accoglie appena sbarcati in Isola), which matches the register point sitting close to the island's landing point. NOTE FOR WRITER/CURATOR: register's scientific name is Phoenix theophrasti Greuter, which is the Cretan Date Palm, not the common Phoenix canariensis usually called 'palma delle Canarie' in Italian; this mismatch between the Italian common name and the Latin binomial is in the register data itself and is worth a second look before publishing (may be a genuine, unusual specimen, or a register labelling quirk). Stands on the same island as the already-published Olive Tree of San Servolo (ven_006), about 184m away; both entries can share the island's access/transport info. No photo hunted (out of scope for this pass, do not verify via photos).
